dedupe_keys.name: eia planned refinery outages in the united states reports 2010 to 2018

description: The Planned Refinery Outages reports assessed whether scheduled maintenance outages at US petroleum refineries could cause shortfalls in the supply of gasoline, jet fuel and distillate fuel relative to expected demand, nationally and in each US region. The analysis simulated regional monthly supply from assumptions about refinery operations and planned outages. They were produced by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The page read holds the fourth-quarter 2018 report, released on 29 October 2018, which found that planned outages were unlikely to cause shortfalls despite near-record gasoline demand, and lists previous issues back to late 2010, published roughly twice a year. Reports are free as web pages with full PDF reports, under EIA's public reuse terms. Caveats: no report newer than 2018 is listed, so the series is treated as archived, and the reports summarise capacity offline, not publishing refinery-level outage data. For simulation it documents a method and historical results for testing whether refinery maintenance or disruption leaves regional fuel supply short, useful in capacity planning and resilience models of fuel supply chains that serve transport and emergency services. It is related to the EIA refinery capacity report record in this catalogue, which lists the plants.
